newsitem.title: FRANCE: Belgian 97 deficit may be under 2.9 pct GDP-Dehaene.
newsitem.headline: Belgian 97 deficit may be under 2.9 pct GDP-Dehaene.

text.p: Belgium's 1997 budget deficit may be smaller than the planned 2.9 percent of gross domestic product, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said in a newspaper interview.

Dehaene also told the French daily Le Figaro in an interview due to appear on Wednesday that he felt certain the European Union would create the planned single European currency in 1999, saying failure would lead to "major disorder".

"Our 1997 budget foresees a deficit of 2.9 percent and we will perhaps even do a bit better," Dehaene said. One EU criterion for joining the single currency from 1999 is a budget deficit of three percent of GDP or less.

Last month, Belgian Budget Minister Herman van Rompuy said the government was on track to reduce the 1997 deficit to around 2.9 percent of GDP. Belgium's High Finance Council, a government advisory body, forecast the deficit will be around 2.8 percent.

Dehaene, who will meet French President Jacques Chirac in Brussels on Wednesday at the start of an official two-day visit, said "there is practically no possible going back" on the single currency because preparations were so far advanced.

"The entire economy and the markets are aimed towards the arrival of the euro. Not getting there -- something I cannot imagine -- would be to create major disorder and to sign away the economies of our countries," he said.

"The euro is the great idea of the end of this century," he added. "Perhaps it has been too reduced to accountancy standards. What's really at stake is European integration and the place of Europe in a world of globalisation."
Asked whether the euro would be possible if France failed to qualify, Dehaene said:

"That would certainly not be the ideal solution. The euro should be created with the participation of France and Germany. But that's not written anywhere in the Maastricht treaty. If a sufficient number of countries meets the criteria, the single currency is due to be set up."
